title: subtree matching or maybe use getParseData(..., includeText=TRUE)
description:
I am working on some linters that require matching a (sub-)tree to the parse tree, e.g. `1:length(expr)`, `x == NA`, etc. 

It would be nice to have some generic solution for this. 

One nice solution would be to implement a (labeled) subtree isomorphism algorithm, and then you could just declare that you want all sub-expressions that have a tree like `1:length(expr)`, where `expr` is an `expression` token.

But this is relatively difficult, and might be slow in R. igraph has algorithms for this, although not tree specific, but still quite fast for trees. But I don't want to bring back the igraph dependency.

So I am leaning towards a more hackish solution. E.g. it would be easy to search for the text of a subtree, using regular expressions, and then do some extra checks. E.g. for `1:length(expr)` you would need to search for `1:length[(](.*)[)]` in `parsed_content$text`, and then check that the captured group is an `expr` token and a grandchild of the matched expression. The drawback of this solution is that the regexp has to be resistant to whitespace, i.e. for the `1:length()` checker it should be rather something like `1\\s*:\\s*length[(](.*)[)]` and this can be painful and easy to mess up. Not to mention cases like `1 : # comment \n length(x)`, which are hard even with the subtree matching.

Also, the hackish solution would need the text of all subtrees. Would you consider calling `getParseData` with `includeText = TRUE`?

title: Allow specifying default lint settings
description:
There are a few options for this.
- Global Settings
  - Just have a global config file somewhere
  - Contributing to packages with different settings may be annoying
- Package specific settings
  - Put the config in the DESCRIPTION
    - from http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#The-DESCRIPTION-file it says `There is no restriction on the use of other fields not mentioned here (but using other capitalizations of these field names would cause confusion)`
    - downside is this only works if you are developing a package, also I don't know if CRAN will be happy with this
  - Put them in the Rstudio project file
    - Allows use with any Rstudio project, so doesn't have to be a package
    - but you have to use Rstudio.
  - Use our own config file
    - Further pollutes the directory with a new file
    - Have to add it to .RBuildIgnore
    - However this might be easier to link to or contributers to find

title: feature suggestion: cache
description:
Running `lint` on large files (like editing an R script with a few hundreds/thousands of lines and saving often with a hook automatically calling `lint`) can result in pretty decent CPU load, which might be avoided by introducing some caching algorithm.

I could imagine at least two options to do so:
- saving the results of `lint` of each R expression in a file named to the hash of the R expression
- storing the results of `lint` of each file along with the last version of the file and run `lint` only on the parts highlighted in the diff

Probably the first option is easier to implement, e.g. that's what I'm doing with my `evals` function in `pander` relatively easily, although the user can choose if the cache should be stored on disk (permanent) or in an hidden R environment (fast but temporary).

title: `lint()` fail when called from LSP with `text` argument and the name of a file not yet saved.
description:
Hello. I don't know if this is specific to my setting, but I'm getting some odd errors while trying `lintr` for the first time via Neovim's LSP (with the `R.nvim` plugin and the `languageserver` package).

If open a new R file in a _buffer_ with a name set to it but not yet saved to disk (e.g. either calling `nvim not_saved.R` from the command-line or calling `:e[dit] not_saved.R` from inside Neovim), `lintr` immediately starts to complain:

> ```not_saved.R|1 col 1 error| Failed to run diagnostics: ! in callr subprocess. Caused by error in `lint_impl_(linters, lint_cache, filename, source_expressions)`: ! Linter `linter()` failed in '/home/(...)/not_saved.R': Caused by error in `normalizePath()`: ! path[1]="/home/(...)/not_saved.R": No such file or directory```.

An unnamed buffer doesn't trigger this message though.

I _believe_ the LSP is calling something like `lintr::lint(filename = "/path/to/not_saved.R", text = "")` (or `text = "\n"`), passing the associated file name as an identifier of some sort. Calling the function like this directly from R generates the same error message:

```r
> lintr::lint(filename = "not_saved.R", text = "x = 1")
Error in `lint_impl_()`:
! Linter `linter()` failed in not_saved.R:
Caused by error in `normalizePath()`:
! path[1]="not_saved.R": No such file or directory

R > rlang::last_trace()
<error/rlang_error>
(...)
---
Backtrace:
     ▆
  1. └─lintr::lint("not_saved.R", text = "x = 1")
  2.   └─lintr:::lint_impl_(linters, lint_cache, filename, source_expressions)
  3.     ├─base::withCallingHandlers(...)
  4.     └─lintr:::get_lints(...)
  5.       ├─lintr:::flatten_lints(linter_fun(expr))
  6.       │ └─lintr:::flatten_list(x, class = "lint")
  7.       └─lintr (local) linter_fun(expr)
  8.         └─lintr:::find_package(source_expression$filename)
  9.           └─lintr:::normalize_path(path, mustWork = !allow_rproj)
 10.             └─base::normalizePath(path = path, winslash = "/", mustWork = mustWork)

```

Yet, using _any_ valid path like `/dev/null` or `/etc/shadow` works:
```r
 > lintr::lint("/dev/null", text = "x = 1")
/dev/null:1:3: style: [assignment_linter] Use <- for assignment, not =.
x = 1
```
